content.text: The cost models agree — my test had wrong per-run counts (`[1,0,0,2]` vs actual `[0,1,0,1]`). Let me fix and re-verify:

arguments.command:
cd /workspace && python3 - << 'EOF'
import sys
sys.path.insert(0,'/workspace/tmp/tests')
import brutelib
routes = {(0,0):0,(0,128):1,(1,128):2,(2,128):3}
routes2 = {(0,0):0,(1,128):2,(2,128):3}
runs = brutelib.compile_runs(routes)
starts=[s for s,_ in runs]
bl=[(3,[1,1,1,2]),(11,[3,0,0,0])]   # v0 bursts
b1 = brutelib.brute_full(starts, bl, 2, 1, 9, [0,1,2])
assert b1 == brutelib.brute_pruned(starts, bl, 2, 1, 9, [0,1,2])
runs2 = brutelib.compile_runs(routes2)
starts2=[s for s,_ in runs2]
bl2 = [(5,[0,1,0,1])]               # v1 burst: runs 1 and 3
b2 = brutelib.brute_full(starts2, bl2, 2, 1, 9, [0,1,2])
assert b2 == brutelib.brute_pruned(starts2, bl2, 2, 1, 9, [0,1,2])
print("v0:", b1)
print("v1:", b2)
comb = brutelib.combine([b1,b2], 2)
pages_const = 2 * (1 + (4*4+63)//64)
print("combined:", comb, "-> objective", (comb[0], comb[1]+pages_const), "(expect 135, 9)")
EOF
